findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the PIC could not locate the signed employee health reporting agreements. The PIC was provided with blank copies for all employees to sign today. The signed agreements should be stored in a location where they are always available upon request. The inspector will follow-up on 9/2/2025 to check that the employee health reporting agreements have been signed by all employees.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of debris inside of the ice machine (THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION) and ice bucket at the bar. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. The inspector will follow-up on 9/2/2025 to check that the ice machine and ice bucket have been cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed there are a significant number of flies at the facility within the kitchen. The facility grills outside and flies enter the facility when the door is opened and closed. The inspector suggested various solutions, such as fly strips near the doorway (must be placed away from food contact surfaces), air curtains, mesh netting over the door, and contacting a pest control company for more recommendations. The inspector will follow-up on 9/2/2025 to check on flies in the kitchen.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: 

(1) The food debris on the bottom shelf of the freezer in the kitchen and single door freezer in the outside dry-storage shed. 

(2) The dust on the shelves holding clean dishes above the triple sink. 

(3) The dust and grease on the vent in the kitchen ceiling. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that the PIC could not locate food handler certificates for all employees. Ensure that all employees have basic food handler training and certificates are kept at the facility by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed the facility did not have employee health reporting forms. The PIC (person-in-charge) was provided with blank copies during the inspection. Every employee must sign the employee health reporting forms. There will be a follow-up on 08/30/2024 to ensure that the reporting agreements have been signed by all employees. 

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed raw meat stored above cheese in the standing cooler. The raw meat was moved below the cheese during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always stored according to their proper storage order to prevent cross contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the inside of the bar ice machine has an accumulation of soil residues. Food contact equipment must be cleaned to sight and touch to avoid contamination. There will be a follow-up on 08/30/2024 to ensure the inside of the ice machine has been cleaned. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed cheese and milk in the standing cooler that was not date marked. TCS foods held at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum (the day the food was opened is considered day 1, food is discarded after 7 days). The foods were date marked during the inspection. Ensure that all TCS foods held in the facility longer than 24 hours are date marked. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed meat being thawed sitting in still water when the inspector arrived. The PIC was instructed to turn on the faucet to create continuous running water and partially open the drain. The PIC was educated on proper thawing techniques. Ensure that TCS foods are always thawed using an approved method. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed single use articles (serving paper) being stored in a box on the floor. Single-use articles must be stored at least 6-inches above the floor to prevent contamination. The PIC moved the single-use articles off the floor and onto a table during the inspection. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed the facility is using Purell food service surface sanitizer spray bottles as sanitizer. The PIC stated they had the proper test strips in the past, but they are currently out of test strips. They began the process of ordering new test strips during the inspection. There always need to be test strips available to accurately measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions. There will be a follow-up on 08/30/2024 to ensure that test strips are available. 

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.
